exposure: change in blood pressure measurements during pregnancy
cohort: The study included women diagnosed with pre-eclampsia, categorized into those with eclampsia, those with pre-eclampsia complicated by pulmonary oedema, and pre-eclampsia controls without end-organ complications, all from a large referral center in Cape Town.
finding: Increased systolic blood pressure at pre-eclampsia diagnosis was associated with pulmonary oedema, and increased diastolic blood pressure at diagnosis was associated with eclampsia, but early pregnancy blood pressure measurements were not useful as risk factors for these complications.
